sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: Does the relation x = y², for real y define y as a function of x? Justify the decision.
choices: Yes; repeated outputs are allowed, only repeated inputs with different outputs are not.
No; the input 1 is paired with both 3 and 8.
No; the input 4 gives both y = 2 and y = −2.
Yes; each input appears once, so each has exactly one output.

items.prompt: A machine starts with 120 components and consumes 4 per hour. It can run for at most 15 hours. What is the domain of C(h) = 120 − 4h in this context?
A sequence is defined by a(1) = 4 and a(n) = a(n − 1) + 6 for n > 1. Find a(5).

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: In a modelling context, the graph of a cooling object’s temperature flattens out towards a horizontal line. Which feature is this, and what does it mean?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
